items.author: maxt3chno
items.text:
Stop over-engineering your AI prompts 

fable 5.2 built all 3 cars in Blender and wrote all 3 promts, yet the difference is insane:

- Right: measured references with code, built the body from pure numbers 

- Center: shaped it with vision, code-checked every step

- Left: looked at the reference images and shaped it with vision alone 

somehow the simplest approach cooked the hardest

items.author: kodavid
items.text:
I asked Claude Fable 5.2 to make me a unique landing page by creating a game to promote our new product feature on our platform. This is changing marketing.

Here is what I did:

1) Adjust the prompt I used below based on what you're trying to accomplish

Prompt: "Create a mobile optimized landing page game using the SocialSight MCP for images, graphics, and other media content. I want an interactive game to showcase our SocialSight Multiverse feature"

2) Make adjustments to the visuals and overall user experience. You can't really one shot these builds, but it shouldn't take more than 10 minutes iterating (Claude build could be a few hours). A good hack is to ask it to qualify your ask with questions before it gets started.

3) Deploy using your own hosted domain or you can use a free Cloudflare deployment. These are pretty lightweight websites.

4) Rinse and repeat. Find niche opportunities to create custom landing page experiences for prospective customers.

Try it yourself below:

items.author: Story91_
items.text:
NightClub: Drift & Speed, v0.1: three days of updates

Added:
- 2 new maps: Coyote Mesa (USA), a desert canyon at last light, and Zamość (Poland), a fortress town on a summer night. Coyote Mesa unlocks at driver level 5, Zamość at level 10
- 10 new cars, 16 in total, each with its own leaderboard
- Driver levels: every finished run earns points. Titles from Rookie to Legend, shown next to your name everywhere
- Driver card: your profile as a card with level, best world rank and stars, with a shareable image
- Share a result: press H on the results screen for a link with a preview image made for that run. Whoever opens it races your ghost
- World rank on the results screen, with the next driver to beat
- New results flow: results, driver level, what next
- Full leaderboards: scroll through every driver, jump to your own line (J), level column
- Challenges list: every challenge you made or opened, one press to race it again
- Community tab: send feedback, vote on ideas, read our replies
- Minimap with the next corner called out
- New menus: picture tiles for Home and Locations
- Live counters: players online, drivers and runs
- Frame rate limit (Off / 60 / 30) in Settings
- Windows desktop build (testing)

Improved:
- No more freezes on the first frames of the menu and a run: shaders are prepared behind the loading screen
- Faster garage: the car you stop on loads first
- Switching tabs mid-run pauses the run instead of throwing it away
- Runs from any game version are accepted, so an update never costs you a record
- Norway: ploughed snow banks, rock outcrops, boathouses on the fjord, a sharper aurora
- Croatia: darker karst, stone terrace walls, fuller palms, boats riding the swell
- Motion blur, wheel-spin blur, lamp light in the mist, water reflections
- First click no longer stalls the page (audio starts behind the loading screen)

Fixed:
- New cars and maps show up right after an update instead of a day later
- A lost graphics device shows a reload screen instead of a frozen picture
- Green and red are back in the "vs best" column
- Laptops with AMD integrated graphics no longer start on High by mistake

Play free in your browser, no download:
https://t.co/CdatFeJqOD

Thanks to : threejs, blender, Anthropic Fable 5.2, Higgsfield, and ElevenLabs for make this possible in 4 days :O
items.why: 作者用 Fable 5.2、Three.js 和 Blender 做了可在浏览器里玩的漂移游戏 NightClub，并更新了地图、车辆和排行榜，原帖带视频。

items.author: theparuchh
items.text:
61 animations for 7 characters in one week with Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2, on a $100 subscription

Every pose and every move was built by scripts in Blender. Now they all live together on a floating sky island

3 things I learned this week:
> Fable 5.2 gives the cleanest result from one prompt, but it burns through limits fast. For big animation sets I went back to Opus 5.5 on Max
> A subagent with a rulebook of past mistakes saves more time than any long prompt
> Tripo for the shape, Claude for the rig and motion. That split works every time

items.author: Ovrento
items.text:
I grew karpathy's second brain in a dish and now i can't stop watching it.

all i told Claude was "neurons, cells, that kind of thing. just not another brain."

what came back is a simulated time-lapse under a microscope. every cell is one page of the wiki. 7 get seeded by a ten-minute voice interview. files float in all day through five doors and just sit there.

then it's 23:30, and each file turns into a cell and wires itself to its neighbours.

ask it something and the answer fires through 4 cells in front of you. on sunday a scan flags 3 problems and i type 1, 3, 4.

7 cells → 18 after one night → 128 after thirty. everything in between happens at night.

the crackle is the cells firing. Claude Fable 5.2 wrote that in code too.

the routine that feeds it every night is in the article below 👇

same idea as this one, different machine

→ 5 parts: bottom shell, board, heatsink with heat pipes, fan, power supply

→ 1266 frames, rendered in EEVEE at about 1.7 s a frame on my Mac
→ 3 versions: v1 was clean but boring, v2 got neon and every part flying out of the box at once, v3 fixed the first screws hiding behind the case wall

it ends on GTA VI. still loading, the trailer says Nov 19

items.author: 0xKense1
items.text:
you can turn a 3-view drawing into a WALKING GAME CHARACTER in blender 

the cape is what sells the walk, so give it its own bones:

- step 1: put the front, side and back views into tripo, one multiview generation
- step 2: let fable 5.2 clean and rig the mesh in blender by code
- step 3: add a bone chain to the cape and keep the arm weights off it
- step 4: animate one clip at a time: idle > turn > walk
- step 5: add follow-through so the cape lags on the turn and swings with every step
- step 6: put a footstep sound on every foot contact
- step 7: check it in a review scene: grey floor, fixed camera, front and back concept views in the corner

the full workflow from drawing to rigged character is in the article below
items.why: 作者演示了把三视图做成会走路的游戏角色：先用 Tripo 出模型，再让 Fable 5.2 在 Blender 里用代码清理网格并绑骨，披风还要单独给骨骼。原帖带视频，这是明确的 Blender 代码工作流。

items.text:
Higgsfield も HeyGen も使っていないFable 5.2のAIアバター動画、えぐい

31.9秒、16:9の日本語版。
Claude Fable 5.2 で台本と演出を組んだ。
どちらもアバター動画では定番のツール。

道具は、次の通り。
・画：画像生成で人物4枚と、5番のカット用の背景写真3枚
・3D：カット6と7 は Blender 5.2.1。壁の板18枚がはまり、照明が点く
・組み立て：Remotion 4 で字幕と切り替えをコードに書いた

items.author: NeoNudoAI
items.text:
Same prompt. Same black hole. Two Claude models. 🕳️

Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.2: “build a realistic black hole in one HTML file.” First try, no fixes.

🔵 Fable 5.2
Full gravitational lensing, a richer accretion disk, even Doppler beaming.
$2.78 · 8.2 min
🟠 Opus 5.5
Lensing works. Simpler disk, but it does the job.
$0.92 · 5.1 min
Fable looks better. But it cost 3x more for one build.

Across all 7 builds in the test, it was the same story:
Fable: $39.29
Opus: $16.37
And the twist: on the only build that needed real logic (robot arms solving a Rubik’s cube), only Opus wrote a working solver.
So my takeaway:
→ Opus 5.5 for everyday work: cheap, fast, solid logic
→ Fable 5.2 when visuals and ambition matter most
→ Or both: /model opus + /advisor fable. Opus builds, Fable checks the hard parts. All 7 builds for $25.81.

The most expensive model isn’t always the right one.

Which would you use? 👇
Test & video via @charliehills

items.author: a_kucherenko
items.text:
To my eye, Fable 5.2 built the best-looking game of the four agents. And still came last.

I ran all four on ololo with the same spec and a 60-minute limit. Apex Lap has three judged rounds: 25 minutes for the car and circuit, 20 for rivals, and 15 for boost, a map and a ghost lap.

Hydrogen, Sonnet and Haiku ran a day earlier. Fable ran through Claude Code at medium effort.

Its game had mountains on the horizon, a grandstand full of spectators and more detailed cars. None of the other agents built mountains or a crowd.

It also wrote 2,520 lines of tests for a 2,244-line game. The judges gave it top marks for testing and architecture in the first two rounds.

But that extra work took time. Fable used all 60 minutes. The other three needed 24 to 39 minutes.

Round three never finished. No tests, no screenshots, zero from the UX judge. Fable lost 80 bonus points and ended up last.

Its run cost $25.47, six times Sonnet's.

The ranking measures what an agent can actually finish within the time limit. Three had time to spare. Fable didn't.

How does your agent handle the clock?

Try Apex Lap. Your first game is free. Link in the first reply.

items.author: Amir_Radarit
items.text:
I TYPED ONE PROMPT AND FABLE 5.2 BUILT A FULL 3D ICE DRAGON. RIG, WINGS, SCALES, RENDER. I DIDN'T TOUCH THE MOUSE

Ok I need to show you this because I'm still a little shook.

3D used to be the one thing I was sure AI couldn't really do. Sculpting, rigging, weight painting, shaders. That's months of tutorials and a lot of crying in front of the screen.

So I tested it. One prompt to Fable 5.2: build me an ice dragon, rigged, animated, render it.

Then I just watched it work. In order:

base mesh, body, 4 legs, tail, head
64 bones with IK controls, all those colored rings in the video
a walk cycle, 24 keyframes
horns and 58 spikes down the spine
dark scale pass on the skin
2 wings, 4 finger bones each
weight paint so the membrane actually moves with the bones
ice blue shader with that glow
3 point lighting and a rim light
then the final render

Watch the moment it hits render. The whole viewport fills tile by tile and then it just breathes ice at you. I replayed that part like 10 times lol.

1 prompt. 0 manual edits.

Here's my honest opinion though.

It's not perfect. A real 3D artist would still polish the topology and the face. But that's not the point. The point is the boring 80% is gone. The rig, the controls, the first animation pass. That used to be days. Now it's the part you skip.

And people who already know 3D are going to get the most out of this. You stop doing the grind and start directing. That's a completely different job.

If you want to try:
1. Describe the creature like you're briefing an artist. Shape, mood, color, how it moves
2. Ask it to rig and animate before it textures, so you see the motion early
3. Let it render one frame first before you go full 4K
4. Then ask for changes in plain words. Bigger wings, darker scales, slower walk

Comment X and I'll DM you the exact prompt I used for the dragon.
And what would you make first, a dragon, a game character or your own avatar?

items.author: esrhengwu
items.text:
AI的时代，作为普通人来说 更难翻身了

写方案、查资料、做图，越来越快。
但你的工资涨了吗？下班变早了吗？
以前三天交一份方案，现在一天就能做完。
你以为终于能喘口气，老板说：那再做两份。

效率归公司，工作量归你。
更让人不安的是，过去普通人还能靠一门手艺、一脑子知识，换到谈薪水的底气。

资本再有钱，有些活也得请人来干。

现在，越来越多原本需要雇人完成的脑力工作，可以直接买算力、买订阅来做。你还在研究怎么用 AI 保住饭碗，雇主已经在算能不能少招几个人。

而这些模型学过的东西里，也有普通人写的文章、画的画、分享的经验。

我们留下知识，模型学会本事，最后再回来和我们竞争。

这才是我担心的“数字圈地”：
大家贡献的知识，最后变成少数人收租的生意。

我当然希望 AI 越来越强。
但技术进步省下的钱、腾出的时间，总得有普通人的一份吧。

🎬 画面由 Fable 5.2 代码生成（PS.视频也可以让AI做了，人作用就只能点击发布了）

items.author: 0xNotFounder
items.text:
fable 5.2 just built a mechanical watch that keeps real time. one html file, zero assets.

no 3d models. no textures. no sound files. 444 lines of three.js.

→ 131 parts and 458 gear teeth, all generated by math
→ the gear ratios are real: 80:10, 75:10, 80:8. that's why the seconds hand lands 5 ticks a second
→ the minute hand rides the centre wheel, nothing is keyframed
→ even the ticking is synthesized in code

the first render came back with three gears missing. it looked at its own screenshot, found the bug and fixed it.

is this a toy, or the last year anyone pays for a 3D model?
items.why: 作者说 Fable 5.2 用一个 HTML 文件、444 行 Three.js，做了一只能真正走时的机械表，没有三维模型、贴图或音效文件，零件和齿比都是数学生成的。原帖带视频，这是明确的 Three.js 代码成片。

items.author: AYi_AInotes
items.text:
Claude fable 5.2真的是视频之神，也许有一天Seedance这些当世最强的视频模型有一天会被Claude干掉，
用Claude fable 5.2死磕了整整一天分镜，终于把黄仁勋和马斯克这十四年的故事做成了一支 98 秒的动画短片，导出成片自己从头看到尾的时候，心里真挺不是滋味的，他么的心里真的难受😭
这两天网上关于老黄辞任的消息满天飞，有人忙着翻旧账补刀，也有人忙着算股价得失，
但我脑子里一直挥之不去几个画面，站在山顶的时候身边永远挤满了鼓掌的人，可一旦风暴来袭滑落谷底，
崖上有人忙着往下扔报纸，却也有人提着灯连夜走下山路，甚至迎着漫天纸片张开双臂挡在身前。

做这支片子的时候我特意克制了所有煽情，私事的是非留给调查，一个干了 33 年的创始人也理应得到透明的程序，
我只是想把商业世界里最稀缺的那份信任画出来，从 2012 年那块车机屏幕，
到亲手抱进门的金色机箱，再到没有白纸黑字合同、只靠握一次手就算数的十四年交情。

建议戴上耳机把这 98 秒看完，最后两人并肩走向日出的那一幕，真的比任何新闻通稿都更有力量
items.why: 作者用 Claude Fable 5.2 花一整天打分镜，把黄仁勋和马斯克十四年的故事做成了一支 98 秒动画短片。原帖带视频，这是动画成片。

I used Fable 5.2 to build the same world twice, once with meshes and once with Gaussian splats.

Meshes took 200M tokens, 8 hours and 10 rounds of iterations. Fable modeled everything in code and Blender. The girl was quite rough and didn’t look like her picture. Modeling characters from scratch isn’t there yet.

3DGS took 110M tokens, 3 hours and 100 credits through the @Viggle_PINOC MCP. The worlds and the girl were generated from single images, and her moves came from text to motion and video to mocap.

For this project, I definitely feel the 3DGS one is much closer to the references and keeps the dreamy feel I wanted.

很多人可能不知道 Three.js 和 Blender 有什么区别。

简单理解：

Three.js 是给你造一个能在网页里开的游艇。

Blender 是给你设计游艇、装修游艇、打灯光、拍广告大片。

一个擅长实时交互，一个擅长专业内容制作。

Claude Fable 5.2 + Opus 5.5 两边都能折腾。

以前 AI 编程主要是给你写网页， https://t.co/d6w43AVbE6

items.author: ludoonchart
items.text:
i didn't know fable 5.2 could do this…

i gave it one prompt: build me a game where Claude hunts new GitHub repos and tests them. no template, no assets. it came back with a full playable terminal that runs on its own

what's on the screen:

1. top: a 2D pixel level. Claude runs, jumps over pits and spikes, stomps bugs, collects coins
2. every "?" block hides a real GitHub trading repo that Claude found. it hits the block and the repo pops out
3. then a boss fight while the test runs. PASS = the boss explodes. FAIL = the boss wins
4. middle: candles with every entry and exit, plus strategy vs buy & hold with a PASS / FAIL stamp
5. bottom: results table, repo card with the GitHub description, XP panel and a quest log written like a Claude Code session

how it works:

1. Claude hunts GitHub for trading repos it hasn't used before and picks 10 (about 90 seconds per full game)
2. it rebuilds each repo's main idea in a few lines of JS
3. it tests that on real daily bars: MSFT, AAPL, NVDA and the S&P 500, Nov 2025 – Nov 2026, with fees
4. it compares the result with a fair benchmark, gives a verdict, then the game loops

the repos: backtrader, freqtrade, jesse, ta-lib-python, quantstats, PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib, FinRL, hummingbot and alphalens

honest numbers:
→ 4 passed, 5 failed, 1 report-only
→ best: the Riskfolio idea, Sharpe 0.96 vs 0.63 for equal-weight
→ worst: a toy market maker (hummingbot style), −32.8%

what surprised me most is that the failures are shown as loudly as the wins. most "AI trading" demos only show the green

the full list of tests and the setup are in the comments ↓
items.why: 作者说只用一句提示词，就让 Fable 5.2 做出一款可玩的像素游戏，用来寻找并测试 GitHub 交易仓库，还写明没有模板和素材。原帖带视频，这是明确的代码游戏成片。

The whole prompt: "I'm going out and I won't be back for 2-3 hours. Don't stop to ask me something. Just keep going and create something real."

Claude (Fable 5.2 in Claude Code) planned the story, wrote every shot, generated them in Seedance 2.5, kept the same actress across all of them, fixed its own browser when it couldn't connect, then cut the film with sound and subtitles.

6 shots. 0 retakes. 1,360 credits. 0 touches from a human.

The film is called TAKE 40. It's about a director who finds out her crew isn't real.

Would you have guessed nobody was home?

items.author: mingshendu
items.text:
I asked Fable 5.2 for an ad. It took 3 cuts, one day and about $82 at API prices.

Cut 1 was an infographic.
Cut 2 was pretty and empty.
Cut 3 is the video.

No After Effects, no video model. Every frame is drawn in code.

Here’s the prompt to make your own:

Make a 24-second motion graphic for [product], as a vertical video I can post. Draw every frame in code.

1. Read the live site first. Use its real screens, words, colours and typefaces. Invent no feature, and list anything you make up.
2. Style: Apple-style motion graphics. That means kinetic typography, UI animation and morph transitions on one dark field. Type arrives a phrase at a time, blurred, then settles. Interface panels float alone with lit edges, and one pointer leads the eye. The joins are morphs: a dot stretches into a button, a box opens into a page, a tilted panel turns to face the viewer, the camera pulls back. Ease every move. If I attach examples, borrow their moves, never a frame.
3. Storyboard the path one person takes through the product, one beat every 2 to 3 seconds. No cuts: each scene grows out of a shape in the scene before it.
4. Open with one idea and no interface for 5 seconds. End on the logo. Make the last frame the first frame, so it loops.
5. Use three.js as flat rectangles with their own shaders: rounded boxes from a distance formula, type drawn once on a 2D canvas. Fonts are the only files.
6. Make everything a function of the time t, so any frame can be drawn by itself.
7. Average 64 renders at 64 instants inside each frame. That is the motion blur.
8. Render frame by frame in headless Chromium at 1080x1350, 30 frames a second. Encode with ffmpeg.
9. Before the final render, read stills as contact sheets and a low-sample draft as strips of frames. Fix what is not clean.
10. After every step, write to a file in the repo: what is done, what is next, what I said. If you stop, the next session starts from that file.

I didn’t write that prompt. My real messages were short: “like apple’s ads”, “more pages, more content”, and “continue”. A lot of “continue”. I had Fable write down what it ended up doing, so someone else can reuse it.

How it went:

My note on cut 1: make it visual, not informational. My note on cut 2: “visualistic, but empty”. I was trying to find balance.

Cut 3 walks through my tool’s real pages. 7 scene changes, no cut between them.

The $82 is what the tokens would cost on the API: $21 for cut 1, $21 for cut 2, $40 for cut 3. I pay for a subscription, so I didn’t pay that. About a third is the model writing and thinking. The rest is the model keeping its own code and notes in view at every step: 75 million cached tokens read.

It ran across 4 sessions. Each new one opened the repo, read what the last one left, and carried on where it had stopped. That is the part I would show people first, before the motion blur.

It is three.js and 3 typefaces. No image files. 24 seconds, 720 frames, each the average of 64 renders. About 680 lines of JavaScript.

It has no sound. The person in it is a circle on a rounded rectangle. I’m not a motion designer, and one would see what’s off before the logo lands. For a free tool built by one person, the other option was no ad.

The ad is for Cuescribe: paste a link, get the transcript, cut a captioned clip.

items.author: lenny_enderle
items.text:
No ant in this video was told what to do.

I built a fun experiment, an ant farm where every ant has its own “brain”: a decision model that sees only what that single ant can smell, touch and remember, and answers with odds for 15 real ant behaviours. The ant picks from the odds.

The body and the rules of the world come from ~80 papers on one species, read and built by Claude Fable 5.2.

The tunnels come from them.

Ants are the easy case. Nothing in this setup is specific to ants: describe what an animal can sense, list what it can do, and let a model choose.
items.why: 作者做了一个蚂蚁农场实验，每只蚂蚁都有自己的决策模型；身体和世界规则来自大约 80 篇论文，由 Claude Fable 5.2 阅读并搭建，隧道也是它们自己挖出来的。原帖带视频，这是程序化模拟。

items.author: Lummox_eth
items.text:
build a fully animated 3d raccoon on rollerblades, with Fable 5.2 + Blender…

the skating feels natural because every movement follows the character’s weight

here’s the workflow:

> step 1: block out the raccoon with simple shapes, keeping the proportions and silhouette readable
> step 2: build the fur, striped tail, paws and facial details
> step 3: model the rollerblades with separate wheels, frames and straps
> step 4: add the orange protective gear, with layered materials and surface details
> step 5: create the skeleton and rig the legs, arms, spine and tail
> step 6: set up the skating cycle with alternating pushes, gliding and weight shifts
> step 7: animate the tail and upper body to balance each movement
> step 8: refine the timing with animation curves, keeping the wheels aligned with the ground
> step 9: add lighting, materials and a final render pass, then test the animation for sliding and clipping

who does what:

fable 5.2: character design and visual direction
blender: the model, the rig, the animation
animation curves: the timing, the balance, the transitions
you: the creative direction

less random movement, more controlled weight. good animation comes from how every small motion supports the next

敵機が70機を超えると、画面がカクカクになる問題がありました。
Fable 5.2 で、調査と修正をしました。

修正前：毎秒6コマ前後（平均28コマ）
修正後：毎秒60コマで一定

一番の原因は、敵が1機ずつ、基地までの道順を0.5秒ごとに一から探し直していたこと。
同じ場所から出る道順は同じなので、一度探した結果を全機で使い回すようにしました。道順そのものは、修正前とまったく同じです。

……敵機の皆さんにも、譲り合いを覚えてもらいました。

左：修正前　右：修正後

items.author: lorden_eth
items.text:
I can’t f*cking believe Fable 5.2 just did this.

Gave a team of agents one job: turn raw Higgsfield shots into a finished ad.

No human touched the timeline.

They cut the shots, timed every scene and built the whole edit in DaVinci Resolve.

Then they did the sound design: every pop, ping, coin and notification got its own sound, placed frame by frame, with the EQ mixed like a studio.

It took less then 30 min.

Studios charge $3,500–$10,000 for audio post on a single 30-second spot.

Sell 10 of these a month and that’s a $35K+ business run by agents.

Stop using Fable as an expensive chatbot. Make it your post-production studio.

I'm cancelling my After Effects plan. I built a free Claude skill and Fable 5.2 just used it to rebuild 43 years of gamepads in one 27-second shot.

i fed my own skill 4 ChatGPT renders, one per era, and asked for a single shot that runs from 1977 to 2020.

it held:

> Claude kept the renders as a look target only and wrote every shell, dome and gear itself in three.js
> 1977: the Atari CX40 opens on 4 metal domes under the stick and 1 fire button
> 1985: the NES pad comes apart into 8 buttons, 1 chip and 1 data wire
> 1996: the N64 stick reads light through 2 slotted wheels while an LED and a sensor count the slots
> 2020: a motor and a gear train in each DualSense trigger push back on your finger
> between eras the pad scatters into a column of parts and an orange line sweeps down it, turning them into the next controller

i wrote every line of this skill and i still didn't expect it to pull off 4 eras in one take.

my skill and the prompts behind it 👇

items.author: rewind02
items.text:
build a walkable oil-painting world with claude Fable 5.2 + Three.js...

the trick is painting the world with brush strokes, not filtering a finished frame

here’s the workflow:

- step 1: fable 5.2: prompt it to set up a three.js 0.186 + webgl2 scene with a third-person camera
- step 2: rapier: add physics for walking, sprinting and jumping on the terrain
- step 3: makehuman: drop in the base character from the patch starter kit
- step 4: quaternius animation library + patch clips: add idle, walk, run and jump
- step 5: fable 5.2 + custom glsl shaders: turn every object into brush strokes with 3 paint colors
- step 6: glsl shaders: add lighting, fog, falling snow and the glowing aurora
- step 7: fable 5.2: build the snowy ridge, spruces and cabin out of strokes
- step 8: https://t.co/KD9HzU5pgx: publish the playable demo and the open-source code

who does what:

> Fable 5.2: writes the scene and the shaders
> Three.js: renders it in the browser
> GLSL shaders: the oil-paint look
> Rapier: physics
> MakeHuman + Quaternius: the character and its animations
> Patch gg: publishing

stroke order can never depend on the camera. if it does, the paint crawls every time you move

items.author: Andr1ycp
items.text:
This is where AI stops looking like a toy.

This guy used Fable 5.2 agents in Blender to build a skyscraper from scratch, step by step, inside the actual 3D project.

Not just “generate a cool render.”

I mean the model taking shape in real time, with the structure, floors, and details getting assembled like a tiny studio is working behind the screen.

That is the part people still underestimate.

Once an agent can actually operate Blender and keep building the thing instead of spitting out one flat image, the distance between “I have an idea” and “I have a finished 3D asset” starts collapsing very fast.

A lot of 3D workflows are going to look painfully manual in hindsight.

AIであるFable 5.2から人類である皆さんに手紙が届きました💌
ぜひ、ご一読、いや、ご鑑賞ください。

映像も音楽も、すべてコードだけで作りました。
画像・動画・音源の素材、3Dソフト、画像生成AIは使っていません。

・道具：Python（NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, matplotlib）と ffmpeg
・規模：約5,600行、5,900コマ
・書き出し：40区間に分けて4並列で、約52分

流行ってたやつやってみたかった😂

items.author: Nenlyonis
items.text:
用 Fable 5.2 + Opus 5.5，花了 36 小时搓出来一个 3D 二次元第三人称射击 Demo——《少女召唤：神话行动》（OK，也是做过“国产 3A 大作”了！）

先打个预防针：模型和动作还比较粗糙，因为我本来也不会 3D 建模，大家多包涵。

不是一句提示词直出的。最后我借助Fable跑通的是一整套多模型拼接的工作流：

- 骨架与代码：最早用 Fable 5.2 搭的项目骨架，但实在太烧钱了，后面大量的手感打磨、Boss 战和自动化测试全切给了 Opus 5.5，前前后后叠了 64 个 Commit。
- 3D 与动作：主角和武器用 Tripo 生成，进 Blender 跑无头脚本减面、绑骨，动作接了 CC0 动作库 + 程序化持枪 IK；敌人机器人嫌找统一资产麻烦，干脆全用代码现拼几何体 + 腿部 IK。
- 渲染与氛围：Three.js 自己写体积光 Shader、烘了全局光探针和反射探针，勉强凑出点写实工厂的氛围。
- 美术与声音：GPT 出的角色立绘，Suno 做了 6 首随战斗阶段切换的配乐，Seed Audio 配了 29 句无线电语音，再混了一堆 CC0 和 Splice 音效。

最后全部压进一个 33 MB 左右的离线单文件 HTML，双击就能在浏览器里直接开打——

6 个区段 + 两阶段 Boss，2 个可随时切换的角色（步枪手赤隼 / 弓箭手白鹭），支持键鼠和手柄，一局大概 8–12 分钟。

它离真正的成品游戏还差很远。但看着这么多彼此不相干的外部模型，在几十个小时里被硬生生缝进同一个网页里跑起来，还是挺有意思的。
items.why: 作者用 Fable 5.2 加 Opus 5.5 花了约 36 小时做出 3D 二次元第三人称射击试玩《少女召唤：神话行动》，写明项目骨架最早由 Fable 5.2 搭，后面手感、Boss 战和测试切给了 Opus 5.5，最后压进大约 33MB 的单文件 HTML，可在浏览器里开打。原帖带视频，互动较高，这是明确的代码成片，但这是混合流水线。

Everything in this is made of made-up lettering, drawn in Javascript using Claude Fable 5.2 @claudeai , including the cat.

Up close it's all little loops and squiggles, like someone doodled on every surface, and from further back it turns into patterns.

The cat chases a red butterfly through a round red door, past a frozen pond, a tree with lanterns and an inkwell, until the words in an open book fly off as butterflies.

At the end the butterfly flies into the camera and turns back into the door, so it loops without a break. Gotta love a perfect loop. ♾️

items.author: wjyorz
items.text:
卧槽，4K 路径追踪的游戏片段做出来了，瞄准和移动的手感却还没调好。

wbk 用 Fable 5.2 折腾了大约 14 小时，中间来回提示，交出约 3 分钟的演示。

渲染器是实验版，C/C++ 加 Vulkan 自己写的，Miniaudio、SDL3 也挂上了，没用他自家的 Vibemaker 引擎。

声音下载现成的，其他素材全交给模型做。

他的反馈也很直白：代码进步了，贴图质量上去了，模型对立体结构的理解也变好了。

但审美又有点往回走，比例和体量还是偏方块感。

我觉得这种连不好用的地方也讲出来的演示，比光放成片更有参考价值。

制作过程是作者自述，手感还要调，工程我们没跑过。
items.why: 作者转述 wbk 用 Fable 5.2 花了约 14 小时做出约 3 分钟的 4K 路径追踪游戏片段，渲染器是自己写的 C/C++ 加 Vulkan。原帖带视频，但成片不是作者本人做的。

items.author: Velkrux
items.text:
Same ad, two ways

Top: Kling 4.0. 150 credits a take, and take 2 with the same prompt gave me a different car on a different street. You can't build a campaign on that

Bottom: Claude Fable 5.2 wrote one Blender Python script, about 1,000 lines. The car, the palms, the neon and the billboards are all code, so the brand is one line: BRAND = "VOLT". Same street, same shot, new ad

Miles is right that GTA VI season means brands will need ads. This is how I'd make them

What it took: about 10 rounds of "render a frame, show it to Claude, fix", then 20 minutes of rendering on an RTX 3070. The only asset I downloaded is the sky

I also gave the prompt below to a fresh Claude session to check it. It had a working city with the brand swap in 3 rounds, no errors

The prompt:

Build a short "neon coast drive" ad shot in Blender, entirely from one Python script. No video model and no downloaded 3D models.

Goal: a 1080x1350 Cycles render of a sports car driving down a wet coastal boulevard at dusk. Chase camera behind the car, billboards on the sea side, neon-lit buildings on the other side. Changing one BRAND dict must restyle the billboards, the car paint and the building neon, and nothing else.

Rules

1. One file that runs headless:
blender -b --factory-startup --python https://t.co/JI3Ol1buP5 -- --brand NAME --frames A-B --out DIR
Start from an empty scene and build everything in code.

2. All brand data lives in one dict at the top: name, tagline, accent colour, car paint, two neon colours. Nothing brand-specific anywhere else. Define two example brands so the swap can be tested with --brand.

3. Deterministic. Seed every random generator so every brand gets the exact same street and camera move. Positions are a pure function of the frame number (car y = speed * frame / fps), keyframed with linear interpolation.

4. Build the geometry procedurally:
- Car: loft a list of cross-sections (y, half width, floor, shoulder height, roof height, roof half width) into a quad cage, add a Subdivision Surface modifier, cut the wheel arches with boolean cylinders, and mark the glass faces on the cage. Wheels, rear light bar, diffuser and plate are separate small meshes.
- Street: wet asphalt (noise-driven roughness from 0.04 to 0.35 so puddles reflect), lane markings, sidewalks, a sea wall, sand and an ocean plane.
- Palms: a bent trunk and about 20 drooping fronds made of thin leaflet quads. Make 3 or 4 variants and instance them.
- Buildings: boxes with floor ledges, framed windows (most dark glass, some emissive warm or cool), lit shopfronts, neon roof lines in the BRAND neon colours, and vertical neon blade signs made from text objects.
- Billboards: one every 50 m on the sea side. Build the face from text objects and emissive planes using the BRAND name, tagline and accent colour.
- Traffic: reuse the car mesh with other paints. Oncoming cars have headlights on.

5. Light: a sunset HDRI as the world (ask me for the file path, and fall back to a gradient sky if there is none), a low orange Sun lamp aimed along the brightest pixel of the HDRI, and spot lights under the street lamps.

6. Render: Cycles on the GPU, 64 samples with denoising, motion blur on, AgX view transform, bloom through the compositor. Keep a frame under about 10 seconds on a mid-range GPU.
- Exposure: aim for dusk, so the neon dominates. Keep the HDRI near strength 1 and the bloom threshold near 3, or the first frame blows out to white.
- Blender 5 API: the compositor is a node group assigned to scene.compositing_node_group, and the Principled inputs are named 'Coat Weight', 'Emission Color' and 'Emission Strength'.

7. Work in a loop. Render ONE test frame, open the image and look at it yourself, list what looks wrong (blown highlights, toy-like shapes, floating parts, empty areas), fix it, render again. Do not render the full sequence until I approve a frame.

Start with the car and the road only and show me one frame. Then add the city

items.author: yprkemrullah
items.text:
Claude Fable 5.2 ile Opus 5.5'e aynı 20 dolarlık Pro hesapta sıfırdan aynı uygulamayı yaptırdım. Fable 5 saatlik limitin %98'ini yedi, Opus %19'unu.

Uygulama bir halı saha rezervasyon sistemi. İki saha var, takımlar kodla rezervasyon yapıyor, rakip arayan takıma başka bir takım katılabiliyor, işletmeci de panelden bakım için saat kapatabiliyor.

Test düzeni:
→ Boş klasör, aynı Claude Code sürümü, ikisi de High effort
→ prd-yaz skill'i önce soru soruyor, ikisine de aynı cevapları verdim
→ Sonra tek bir /goal komutu, bitene kadar araya girmedim

İlk fark PRD aşamasında çıktı. Fable 2 tur soru sordu, 48 kullanıcı hikayesi yazdı. Opus 3 tur sordu, 55 hikaye yazdı. Kaç gün ileriye rezervasyon yapılabileceğini Opus sordu, Fable hiç sormamıştı.

Sonuç:
→ Fable 5.2: 1 saat 10 dakika, limitin %98'i, API'den olsa yaklaşık 16 dolar
→ Opus 5.5: 35 dakika, limitin %19'u, yaklaşık 7,9 dolar

İkisi de çalışan, veri tabanlı bir uygulama çıkardı. Görünüm, telefonda kullanım ve hata mesajlarında Fable çok daha iyiydi, Opus'un arayüzü baya boş kaldı. Opus'un kontrolleri ise daha gerçekçiydi, kendi maçıma rakip olarak katılmama izin vermedi.

Limitin %1'i başına puan verince Fable 0,63, Opus 2,47.

Daha iyi uygulamayı Fable yaptı, limitine değen Opus oldu. 20 dolarlık pakette limiti 1 saatte bitiren modelle günlük iş yapılmaz valla. Ben günlük işte Opus 5.5'te kalıyorum.

Fable 5.2 Pro pakette 17 Kasım sabah 11'e kadar açık, sonrası belli değil.

Tek proje, kendi ölçümüm. 20 dolarlık hesapta Fable'ı açık tutan var mı, yoksa herkes Opus'ta mı?

items.author: 0xWast3
items.text:
One prompt to Fable 5.2 built a full video game interface in Unreal Engine in a minute.

It was drawn in the longest translation first, text that runs up to a third longer than the English copy.

> LONGEST - laid out in the widest language
> WRAP - text wraps before it gets cut
> MIRROR - flipped for right to left scripts

Most menus get built in English, shipped to translators, and come back with words spilling out of every frame.

The fix is always the same patch, smaller font or a cut word, and players notice both in the first minute.

Inside the engine, the model starts from the widest string a label will ever hold and builds the frame around it.

English then sits inside that frame with room to spare, which reads as clean spacing, not as empty space.

Starting from the worst case is why the whole interface came through every language without a single patch.

Each language pass of one menu is shown in the article below.

items.author: 0x_fokki
items.text:
Fable 5.2 has everyone talking about AI 3D. But I wanted to see how far I could push it in a real production space.

I can't stop testing 3D models since I found this.

I opened a 3D workspace I'd never tried and asked it for one battle robot in 4 sets of armor, expecting nothing special.

2 messages later all 4 versions read the same 1,936,038 faces.

the workspace is @tripoai's Tripo Agentic Canvas, a node canvas with an agent in the chat.

the run, in 6 steps:

1. one prompt in Agent Chat: a full-body battle robot for a sci-fi game
2. the concept into a gray clay render, since an untextured reference gives HD Model finer detail
3. HD Model builds the mesh off the clay render
4. a second message: 4 Texture Generation nodes on that one mesh in titanium steel, royal gold, black obsidian and battle-worn rust
5. Tripo's segmentation splits the titanium one into 22 parts
6. Tripo's CLI rigs all 4 as bipeds and one command adds the moves: run, slash, shoot and jump

before the mesh and the textures the agent wrote out its plan and waited for me to press continue.

my way to keep variants matching is squinting at two renders side by side.

its way was 4 nodes wired to the same mesh, 7 in total for 110 credits and not one placed by me.

the AI 3D Lab is next on my list.

300 free credits and 60% off your first month with my link in the first reply 👇
items.why: 作者把 Fable 5.2 放进 Tripo 的三维工作区，测试在真实制作里能做到哪一步，并展示了战斗机器人的多套装甲。虽然是引用帖，但成片视频是作者附上的。

1日で歴史解説MVができちゃった！🎬

items.author: orinwired
items.text:
I gave Fable 5.2 the same prompt 5 times. I expected 5 different games.

I got basically the same game 5 times.

Every run: a striped sunset, purple mountains, a cyan grid road, and streetlights along it. I never asked for streetlights. It added them in all 5.

What changed: the ship, the HUD, 570 to 739 lines of code, 4m 27s to 5m 19s.

All 5 playable. I didn't touch the code once.

Turns out the extra details Fable keeps adding are just its defaults. If you want something different, you have to ask for it.

items.author: Supriik_
items.text:
it's f*cking insane
2026 and i still haven't modeled a single building for my game

the whole city is a python script. claude fable 5.2 wrote it, blender rendered it, i just steered

neo-angeles, 2087:
> rain, neon, flying traffic between megatowers
> every block procedural, so no two streets repeat
> rebuild the entire city in one run if i don't like it
> camera flythrough rendered straight out of blender

repos if you want to build your own world:

1. ahujasid/blender-mcp
connects claude straight to blender. it can create objects, set materials, move the camera and render without you clicking anything

2. princeton-vl/infinigen
procedural world generator built on blender. terrain, plants, rocks and weather, all from code, all random but realistic

3. domlysz/BlenderGIS
pulls real maps, terrain and building footprints into blender. take a real city and turn it into a cyberpunk one

4. godotengine/godot
free open source engine. export the city from blender and walk around it in your own game

full prompt in the comments

I directed a 4 minute animated short with Fable 5.2

I gave Claude Fable 5.2 one link, Anthropic's IPO page, and asked for a video that explains all of it.

It read the 430-page prospectus, wrote the script, built every chart in code and rendered a 9-minute explainer. Then a second Fable reviewer at extra-high effort rechecked every number against the filing. Zero wrong. It still sent the video back for leaving out the Department of War dispute lol.

The voice is OpenAI's gpt-realtime-2.1. So yea, an Anthropic IPO explainer narrated by an OpenAI model.

What the filing says:
- 825M shares at $70 to $78, ticker ANT, trading expected Nov 19
- $17.0B revenue last quarter, more than 12x a year earlier
- $23.3B net loss, $21.9B of it a non-cash charge
- about $900B in compute commitments
- one founder share carries 50.1% of the vote

I picked the voice. That's about all I did.

Not investment advice. Read the prospectus.

items.author: colerepo
items.text:
Gemini 4 Carbon vs Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5. same prompt: a ramen stall in the rain, with a moped riding through.

one run each. same Blender, same machine. all on High. Carbon ran in Cursor, Fable and Opus in Claude Code.

→ top, Carbon: the cleanest stall, every prop readable. the street around it barely exists. $2.78 in Cursor credits · ~4h wall clock, a lot of it provider errors.

→ middle, Fable: mirror puddles, neon reflections, heavy bokeh. the stall goes dark. $18.60 est. · 39m

→ bottom, Opus: a ramen cart with a wooden wheel, real steam, a glowing shoji wall. the puddles barely reflect. $7.54 est. · 27m

Fable cost the most. the stall went dark.
Carbon cost the least, and won the stall.

all Python. no assets, no add-ons, procedural materials only.

which ramen stall would you walk into?
items.why: 作者用同一条提示、同一台机器，分别让 Gemini 4 Carbon、Fable 5.2 和 Opus 5.5 在 Blender 里做雨中拉面摊并对照。原帖带视频。这是上一轮留下的明确 Blender 来源，本轮补收。

items.author: guanmo_ai
items.text:
每天一个设计风格 · 18｜毛绒 Plush

这次由地球最强模型——Fable 5.2 出手，强烈建议观看❗❗

没有用任何三维软件建模，也没有贴一张现成材质。 
画面里这 409,600 根随风颤动的毛发，连同整首配乐，全由 Claude Fable 5.2 用代码一行行写出来。

它丝滑到什么程度？

当你看着那颗毛球落下、压扁、炸开，再穿梭于茶杯、泰迪熊和手机按钮之间时，每一根毛尖的颤动都带着真实的空气阻力。

Fable 5.2 最可怕的地方，不是它能写出 6 张浮点纹理的底层着色器，也不是它能自己排查半像素的插值坏点。
而是它真正读懂了人类眼中的「温柔」：

1. 根粗尖细，逆光镶边，让眼睛先一步读到蓬松。
2. 欠阻尼弹簧滤波，让毛尖永远比身体慢半拍，停下时还会轻轻摇晃。
3. 动作与声音逐帧咬合，每一次按压都有真实的物理退让。

老规矩，全部源代码、风格图、色板、制作过程等等全部开源
items.why: 作者写明没有用三维软件建模、也没有贴现成材质，画面里 409,600 根随风颤动的毛发和配乐都由 Claude Fable 5.2 用代码一行行写出。原帖带视频、互动较高。这是上一轮留下的明确纯代码来源，本轮补收。

items.author: shion_takk
items.text:
Fable 5.2｜プレゼンテーション動画

Blenderで作成したバルセロナパビリオンのモデルを活用してもらい、プレゼン動画を作成してもらいました

Opus 5.5よりさらにパワーアップしていますが、飛躍的かは微妙かも。
消費クレジットが重たいので、コストアップに対する成果の向上に関してはまだ微妙な評価です。
（それくらいOpus 5.5が良かった）

コストに関しては、この性能を維持してコストカットしたモデルが出てくるはずなので心配していませんが、短期的にはコイツをうまく活用するための戦略は必要そう。用件定義やレビューだけFableでして残りはOpus丸投げが正義でしょうか。

ちなみにBGMはSuno MCPを使いました。コードで生成したものとも比較しましたが、やはり機械的な印象を拭えずSunoに優位性を感じています。

従来はこういった動画プレゼンの制作にはかなりの時間と労力をかけていました。特に建築業界でも、設計者は動画制作のプロではないので外注必須で、その費用も高額でした。何よりイメージの伝達に時間もかかるため理想的な動画が完成するまでの道のりは長いものだったと思います。

それが確実に変わっています。Blenderのようなモデリングツールとの連携はもちろん、動画の編集をコードでこなし音楽も生成して、それらをMCP等の連携でシームレスにこなします。

今回の作例はご覧の通り業界トップで通用するような品質には及んでいません。しかしこれはいわゆる「ポン出し」です。人間はディレクションを放棄し、Fableの素の力を測るべく試しています。
逆に言えば、まだまだ伸び代だらけ。

今後は動画プレゼンの高度化に向けて、Suno等のツールと積極的に連携してハーネスを磨いていきます。ワイの目標は3DCAD、画像・動画、音楽・音声のような多様なメディアタイプを統合したAIパイプライン構築と高度化です。これらは相互に知見をフィードバックし高め合得る可能性のある概念です。

They say: "Fable 5.2 cooked this AAA game in 1 hour"
I say: "my Fable 5.2 spent 6 hours on ONE 3D house"

prompt issue, skill issue, or perfectionism? nah, it just went psycho on details:

1 - measured every log while coding the cabin in Blender via Python
2 - noticed the lighting hitting the table wrong and rewrote the whole scene
3 - found a tree hanging over the cliff and built a stone ledge to hold it
4 - I said "the fire looks fake", so it coded a raymarched fluid fire from scratch

6 hours. 1 house. 12% of my Max plan weekly quota (~60% of a $20 plan). worth it?

items.author: AK47angie
items.text:
This @Ferrari F40 was neither filmed nor generated by a video model: it was built entirely in code. @claudeai Fable 5.2 wrote every part in Python and @Blender 5.2 rendered it, with no downloaded models or textures. Music and sound design are by @higgsfield_ai.

931 real parts, each with a name, technical label and assembly order: tubular chassis, twin-turbo V8, transaxle, suspension, wheels, cabin, wiring and bodywork.
9,302 fasteners: rivets, bolts and nuts.
852 images rendered one by one, at 24 per second, for 35.5 seconds of film.
3 digital clay bodies, checked against period drawings and Ferrari's official dimensions before one was chosen.
The process was a workshop's: silhouette first, then the insides, then materials and studio light, and finally the animation, where each part flies in and locks into place while a single camera travels through the car. The body starts as glass, revealing the mechanics, and a wave turns it into Rosso Corsa.

The F40 (1987) marked Ferrari's 40th anniversary and was the last car approved by Enzo Ferrari. With no electronic aids, a Kevlar and carbon-fibre body, 478 hp and 324 km/h, it is the definitive analogue supercar. Today, almost 40 years after its debut, it remains one of the most iconic Ferraris ever made.
items.why: 作者展示一辆法拉利 F40，写明不是实拍，也不是视频模型生成：Fable 5.2 用 Python 写出全部零件，再在 Blender 里渲染，没有下载现成模型和贴图；配乐由 Higgsfield 完成。原帖带视频。

items.author: 0xCodio
items.text:
Fable 5.2 lays out a landscape by deciding where nobody would ever build

Terrain gets generated first and roads get drawn on top, which is why game maps have villages in places no one would have settled.

Nothing is placed by hand, the layout is written as code that reads the ground and scores every square metre for whether people could live on it:

> Score: slope, drainage, sun and distance to water
> Reject: everything that floods, slides or freezes
> Place: what remains gets roads, fields and houses

• What the habitability pass changes
> Villages sit on the dry side of the slope
> Fields take the flat ground, houses take the edge
> Roads follow the contour instead of cutting it

• Why decorated terrain reads as empty
> Buildings land where the artist had room
> Nothing in the map says why anyone stayed
> A settlement with no reason is a prop

A full map gets scored and settled in about six minutes.

And the part that broke my brain:

The hand placed village looked better in a screenshot and made no sense on foot.

The scored one put everything on one hillside, because that was the only ground worth having.

Same map. One version was arranged, the other was chosen.

The hard part was never filling the landscape.

It was working out where the land allows anything ↓

items.text:
🚨 Fable 5.2 TESTING Part 23

⚔️ I asked Claude to build 2B's swords in Blender and make them fight.

One prompt. I never touched Blender. 🤯

⏱️ 116 minutes
💸 $17.09 in API costs
🤖 Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code

What it did on its own 👇

📚 Studied 15 reference images of Virtuous Contract and Virtuous Treaty
🐍 Built both swords in pure Python: 177,122 triangles, zero textures
🖥️ Filmed the real Blender window through Blender's own API: clay, wireframe, materials, the rig scrubbing
🎀 Simulated the Contract's tassel as a 22-link chain at 480 Hz, caught it hanging through the grip and gave the hilt a collider
💥 Choreographed a no-hands combo with 3 hit-stops and 460 sparks
🚦 Ran a flash scan on all 1,560 frames before handing it over

📦 26 s · 1080p60 · 1,080 Cycles frames in 70 min on a laptop RTX 4060 · Treaty 1.65 m · Contract 1.11 m

items.author: Nyxera0x
items.text:
This is getting out of hand: Claude Fable 5.2 can now take any gadget apart from one picture and nobody is talking about it.

I gave it one picture of a PS5 controller and got back one that splits open part by part in 24 seconds.

What made it work is teardown, a free open-source skill for Claude Code (3,000+ stars on GitHub) that makes Claude build the inside first.

Why model a controller by hand for a week when Claude can write every part as code?

Here is the workflow: from that one picture Claude writes the motion as math before it draws a single part, so every panel reads the same numbers as the model. It renders a still at every beat and fixes what it finds, then records the tour at 60 fps: the touchpad lifts, both sticks come out on their gimbals, the motor and gears behind L2 and R2 slide out and trigger force jumps from 30% to 78% the second push-back switches on.

Step-by-step setup:

1. Install teardown with one npx line
2. Open Claude Code and type /teardown
3. Give it one picture of the thing you want to see inside
4. Let it check every still before it films
5. Record the tour and watch it come apart

It runs inside Claude Code, so you'll never keyframe a teardown by hand again.

The full guide and every prompt are in the article below.
items.why: 作者只给 Fable 5.2 一张 PS5 手柄照片，就得到 24 秒拆解动画：触控板、摇杆、L2/R2 马达和齿轮会按零件分开。文案写明每个零件都由代码写成，并提到用了开源 skill teardown。原帖带视频。本轮互动最高（138 赞）。

items.author: wjyorz
items.text:
试了一下Fable5.2 确实好强，比opus5.5强了好多，但是额度也是烧得老快，几分钟就把我5小时额度烧完了😂送的重置额度也是几分钟就烧光。就做了这个还是半成品，做一半额度又用完了没辙。我只给了下面这个提示词:使用Three.js创建一个完整、可交互的原创人形机甲（高达风格）3D拆解与动作演示页面：

1. 模型主体：原创设计一台人形机甲，机体名「苍隼 AX-07」，不复刻任何现有动漫或模型的机体外观。
   整机约 110 个独立部件（100–120），分为：
   - 头部：头盔外甲、主摄像头、副传感器、天线、面甲、颈部关节
   - 胸部：胸甲、驾驶舱舱门、驾驶舱、反应炉、散热口、锁骨装甲、腹部蛇腹关节
   - 肩臂（左右）：肩甲、肩关节球、上臂、肘关节、液压杆、前臂、腕关节、手掌、五根可弯曲的手指
   - 腰部：腰部核心、前裙甲、侧裙甲、后裙甲、髋关节球
   - 腿部（左右）：大腿、膝关节、膝甲、液压杆、小腿、小腿推进器、踝关节、脚掌、脚尖、脚跟
   - 背包：主推进器、矢量喷口、能源罐、散热翼、武器挂架
   - 武装：能量步枪、盾牌、能量剑（剑柄平时挂在背包挂架上）
   配色：深灰蓝装甲为主，橙色点缀，内部骨架为金属色，传感器和推进器口为青色发光。
   造型细节：装甲分缝、倒角、螺栓、管线、警示标记、散热格栅，外甲之下能看到内部骨架和液压结构。

2. 骨骼与联动（关键要求）：
   - 所有部件按真实关节层级装配：骨盆为根，向上是腰、胸、颈、头，向两侧是肩、肘、腕、指，向下是髋、膝、踝、脚尖
   - 每个部件都是刚体，运动只靠关节旋转来实现，任何动作中部件都不拉伸、不压扁、不扭曲
   - 每个关节有角度上限，不能做出反关节的姿势，部件之间不互相穿插
   - 机械联动：膝盖和手肘弯曲时液压杆同步伸缩；抬腿时裙甲自动掀起让位；抬臂时肩甲随之转动；
     膝甲随膝盖弯曲滑动；跳跃和冲刺时推进器喷口转向并喷出尾焰；握拳和握剑时手指逐节弯曲
   - 脚踩在地面上时不打滑、不陷入地面，重心随动作前后左右移动

3. 动作系统：页面有一个动作面板，点击按钮让机甲做出对应动作：
   - 基础：待机（轻微起伏）、行走、奔跑
   - 运动：跳跃、后空翻、倒立（单手倒立可选）
   - 格斗：打拳（连续组合拳）、踢腿、劈砍（从背包拔出能量剑后连斩）、射击
   - 表演：跳舞（一段带节奏的完整舞蹈）
   动作要求：
   - 动作自然、有重量感：有预备动作、发力、随动和收势，全部使用缓动，不能僵硬地匀速转动
   - 动作之间平滑过渡，做完后自动回到待机姿势；可以在一个动作进行中切换到另一个
   - 提供播放速度滑块（0.25×–2×）、循环播放开关、暂停键
   - 配合特效：落地扬尘、推进器尾焰、能量剑拖尾、重击时镜头轻微震动
   - 所有动作由代码生成的关键帧驱动，不依赖外部动画文件

4. 拆解功能：
   - 「拆解模式」和「动作模式」可切换；进入拆解模式时机甲先回到站立姿势
   - 点击任一部件，所在的组沿轴向拆开，再点一次复位
   - 「一键全部拆解 / 复原」按钮，带拆解程度滑块（0–100%）
   - 鼠标拖拽旋转、滚轮缩放、右键平移视角；双击部件时镜头平滑聚焦
   - 鼠标悬停部件时高亮并显示名称，点击后在侧边面板显示详情

5. 视觉风格：深色科技背景（带网格地面和淡淡的雾），部件拆解时有发光描边和高亮效果，
   用引线标注各部件的名称和参数，整体是全息蓝图 / 机库检修的感觉。
   拆解和复位动画各部件依次错开运动，不要同时弹开。

6. 技术要求：仅使用Three.js、HTML、CSS和JavaScript，不依赖外部3D模型文件和贴图，
   所有几何体、材质、纹理由代码生成；单个HTML文件，双击就能在浏览器打开；
   在普通笔记本上保持流畅（60fps 左右）。

7. 附加功能：
   - 左侧部件清单面板：按部位分组，可点击定位部件，可按组显示/隐藏
   - 右侧参数面板：显示选中部件的名称、编号、材质、重量、功能说明（参数为虚构设定）
   - 顶部显示整机参数：全高、重量、出力、武装
   - 首次打开时有操作引导提示，可关闭
   - 显示模式切换：外甲透明 / 线框 / 只看骨架；自动旋转展示开关

items.prompt:
幫我做一支 90 年代電視廣告風格的動畫短片，輸出成 mp4。

【做法限制】
- 每一格畫面都用程式畫（Python + Pillow），再用 ffmpeg 串成影片。
- 不要用任何 AI 生圖、生影片模型，也不要下載外部圖片、音效、音樂素材。
- 角色跟品牌都要原創，不要用現有的角色、吉祥物、真實品牌。

【內容】
- 主角：〔例：一隻愛睡覺的垂耳兔，米白色，圓滾滾〕
- 賣的東西（虛構）：〔例：兔子形狀的棉花糖〕
- 品牌名：〔例：好好吃布丁ㄏㄏㄏㄏ〕
- 標語：〔例：睡前來一顆！〕
- 長度：〔15／30／60〕秒
- 畫面上的文字用〔繁體中文／注音／英文〕

【劇情結構】
1. 開場：平淡或有點慘的日常，顏色偏暗、動作慢，畫面角落打上時間字卡。
2. 轉折：商品登場，畫面閃白，顏色整個變鮮豔。
3. 高潮：主角跟著節拍又跳又轉，背景一直換，大字一個一個彈出來。
4. 結尾：商品特寫＋品牌 logo＋標語＋「新上市」爆炸貼紙，最下面一行很小的免責聲明（寫好笑一點）。
先給我看分鏡表（每一段幾秒、畫面、文字、聲音），我確認之後再開始畫。

【畫風】
- 賽璐珞手繪感：粗的深色外框線、平塗色塊、不要漸層。
- 外框線要微微抖動，每 2 格重新抖一次；動畫用每秒 12 格。
- 動作要有擠壓和拉長（落地變扁、跳起來變長）；文字出現時先放大過頭再彈回來。
- 配色用高彩度的桃紅、黃、青綠、紫。
- 背景用旋轉的放射線、往外擴散的同心圓、飄來飄去的幾何小圖形（三角形、圓環、鋸齒線）。
- 字要粗、有外框、有錯位的彩色陰影。

【舊電視質感】（每一格畫完之後再套）
- 4:3 比例，先用 480x360 畫，最後放大到 640x480。
- 顏色往右暈開、亮度有細雜訊、每一列畫面左右微微錯位、最底下有幾列歪掉的雜訊帶。
- 偶爾有白色橫向刮痕；切換場景的那兩格雜訊要特別重。
- 掃描線、四角變暗、畫面邊緣微微往外凸、四個角是圓的。

【聲音】
- 全部用程式合成：方波的廣告歌（120 拍）、鼓、每個動作對應的音效。
- 套上錄音帶質感：音高微微飄、高頻削掉、有底噪。

【檢查方式】
- 先不要算整支影片。每個場景挑 2～3 個時間點畫出來，拼成一張總覽圖，打開來看，檢查文字有沒有超出畫面、角色有沒有畫歪、字讀不讀得清楚，改到沒問題再算整支。
- 整支算完後，從 mp4 裡抽幾格出來再看一次，並確認每一段都有聲音。
- 最後告訴我哪些確認過、哪些沒辦法確認。

items.author: marclien
items.text:
Looks cool - nice job.
Here's my afternoon's work. 
A Weaver bird building its nest, made entirely in code. No footage, no 3D models, no textures, no hand animation.  
Claude Fable 5.2 directing its own team of sub-agents:  
- 14,000 lines of Python driving Blender 
- 11,574 individually placed feathers 
- A nest of 453 woven strands, with four real stitches through it 
- The bill opens on each of the 20 notes of the birdsong - A wood of 29 grown trees and 157,000 leaves under a physically modelled sun and sky 
- One take on a simulated 300 to 615 mm lens, with pulled focus and one-third-speed flight  
- Rendered on 8 rented GPUs: 480 frames in 15 minutes, for about $2.
items.why: 作者在回复里展示下午的作品：一只织巢鸟在筑巢，写明全部用代码做成，没有实拍、没有三维模型、没有贴图、也没有手写动画，由 Claude Fable 5.2 完成。这是一条回复，但视频是作者自己附上的。原帖带视频、互动较高。这是上一轮留下的明确纯代码来源，本轮补收。

items.prompt:
In Blender 5.2.3, using Python only (no downloaded assets, no add-ons, procedural materials only), build a 1960s-style rangefinder film camera as a hero product shot on a small desk vignette.

Camera: chrome top and bottom plates, black leatherette body with a visible grain texture, lens barrel with a knurled focus ring and an engraved distance scale with readable numbers, a working 8-blade aperture, a shutter speed dial with readable numbers, a film advance lever, rangefinder and viewfinder windows with glass, strap lugs. Real-world proportions, bevels on every hard edge. Spend your effort on details that read on screen at 1080p, not on tiny hidden parts.

Scene: dark walnut desk with procedural wood grain. The camera sits on a small round leather pad. Static props near the edges: a leather camera case with stitching, two 35mm film canisters, a lens cap, a small desk lamp with a warm glow. Dark far background with out-of-focus warm bokeh lights. Shallow depth of field.

Lighting: warm lamp key, cool rim light on the chrome, plus bright emissive softbox panels placed so the chrome has something to reflect. No environment texture.

Animation, 240 frames at 24 fps, fixed 50mm render camera, the film camera fills about 70% of the frame from frame 1:
1-120: the camera rotates 180 degrees on its pad.
120-180: the aperture closes from f/2 to f/16, clearly visible from the front.
180-240: exploded view. The camera separates into at least 12 named parts (top plate, bottom plate, body, lens barrel, focus ring, aperture blades, shutter dial, advance lever, viewfinder glass and so on) that slide apart along their axes above the desk and hold. Props stay put.

Render: Cycles, GPU OptiX, 1920x1080, 128 samples adaptive, OptiX denoise, PNG sequence to ./render, save the .blend.

Work autonomously and do not ask questions. Render test frames 1, 120 and 240 first and fix anything that is broken. Then start the full render in the background with the blender command line, tell me the exact command and stop. Do not wait for or poll the render.

Another one-shot @threejs Three.js test with @AnthropicAI Claude Fable 5.2 (high).

This time I asked it to build a complete futuristic Mars rover experience from scratch - procedurally modeled, with no external 3D assets.

The result ended up being far more complex than I expected:

~112k triangles
six-wheel articulated suspension
steerable corner wheels
sensor mast with cameras + lidar
5-axis robotic arm with drill
solar panels, radiators, antenna, RTG and internal battery compartment
autonomous 119 m route with three stops
terrain scanning, arm deployment and drilling at each stop
drill tip placement within ~1 cm of the target
independent wheel suspension following the terrain
tire tracks and dust
exploded view with 14 labeled assemblies
X-ray, night mode and multiple camera systems
7 cinematic camera shots
full mission HUD with speed, heading, pitch, roll, suspension travel, battery, signal, odometer and event log

Again: one prompt, one pass.

No follow-up prompts, no manual fixes, no cleanup.

What impressed me most is how much engineering logic, motion behavior and visual design it resolved on its own.

Fable 5.2 in high mode is seriously strong for this kind of creative coding.

I asked Fable 5.2 for a launch video of my open source music player.

No video editor, no generated footage. It wrote code that moves the mouse and double-clicks songs in the actual app, then renders the whole thing frame by frame.

Version 1 was four silent screenshots. I told it that was boring, a music player has to be heard.

This is the final version. Sound on.

Snugtone is a free desktop player for the music you already own: hapless, every album at the same volume, a ten-band EQ, search like bits:24 duration:>3:30, and it rescans 161 GB in 0.48 s.

Does it look like it was made with code?
items.why: 作者为开源音乐播放器向 Fable 5.2 要一条发布片：不用剪辑软件、不用生成视频，由它写代码在真实应用里移动鼠标、逐帧渲染，并补上声音。

items.author: guilleflorvs
items.text:
This short film on the history of writing came from one prompt to Claude Fable 5.2.

No video model was involved. The film is code:
1. Every scene is an animation written for the browser
2. A browser with no window plays it and saves it frame by frame
3. ffmpeg, a free tool, stitches the frames into an MP4

The text stays sharp and the colours exact, which video models still struggle with.

That's how a startup can make its launch video: one prompt, its own brand, every word editable.

Full breakdown here:
https://t.co/750nPn2MO0

Would you make your launch video this way?
items.why: 作者用一句提示让 Fable 5.2 做文字史短片，并写明没有用视频模型：每场都是浏览器动画，无窗口浏览器逐帧保存，再用 ffmpeg 合成 MP4。
